title: The systems of the catalog, for scripts
note: references/systems-catalog.md is the authority. This file holds the same facts. A citation is prefix:line. The prefixes are in 'sources'. A variant with sourced_range false has no sourced range. The design solver uses only variants with sourced_range true. Each starter set and each variant has the key proof_class: proved (a law covers it and the solver writes it), simulated (a tool writes it and only the simulator checks it), or none (no tool writes it yet). proof_class is the class when the rest of the selection is proved. proof_class_sim_path is the class of a variant when another choice takes the simulation path. tests/test_interview_honesty.py finds each class by a run.

decisions.text: S04 is core. The variant S04.none is permitted only when S22 is the spine.
Each game needs 1 or more presence gates (S07, S08, S09). The default is S08.
An open game with no input has no separate rule. The presence gate covers it.
S10 can fill the S05 slot only when the visitor does not bank.
S24 does not run while the game is closed, by default.
S18 is a separate optional system.
S07 stays a presence gate of the core slot. It is not a core system alone.
The skill has 2 play patterns: continuous and check_in. The interview asks the pattern first. With continuous, S06 is not core (default none) and the presence gate slot is optional.

For continuous: S05 is core with the default S05.manual_then_automate. S24 and S28 are core. S04 is optional, and S04.none is permitted with S29 or S22. A continuous selection with no S28 is refused. check_in keeps D1 to D9.

For continuous: S04.none is also permitted with S28 and with no S29 and no S22. The game is 1 long run to the hard end, and the run itself is the permanent progress. The solver proves it with the laws L1, L2, L3, L8 and L9 (references/balance-math.md, 1 long run with no reset). Ticket 40, repair 3.

play_patterns.name: Continuous play (a desktop or Steam game)
play_patterns.text: The player plays in long sittings: the demo in 1 sitting, the full game possibly in 1 sitting. The game gives no idle or offline benefit. A session is the whole sitting.
play_patterns.note: The generator lines still pay while the game is open. The closed-game parts of PO6 to PO9 are not applicable when the model has no offline gain. The idle bands are the law band 0 to 1, not targets (decision D10: no idle-value targets).

target_bands.name: length to the hard end
target_bands.proven_game: 9 of 11 short games measure 1 to 11 hours (SG:177)

target_bands.name: first purchase
target_bands.proven_game: Shelldiver: 4 to 5 upgrades after each 1 to 2 minute dive (SG:180)

target_bands.name: demo length
target_bands.note: A guide consensus with no conclusive data. A demo of 2 hours or more is flagged: the nearest proof is the 1 to 2 hour Tower Wizard prototype (SG:189).

target_bands.name: extension past the demo
target_bands.rule: each part past the demo adds new content: a new era, area, system or reset mechanic
target_bands.proven_game: new eras, areas and prestige mechanics (SG:185)

target_bands.name: no source
targets: unlocks in the first 10 minutes and the first hour
target_bands.note: The interview marks each of these targets: no source. It gives no band. A designer value is a designer target, not supported by a source: a warning, not a refusal.

target_bands.name: largest gap between unlocks
target_bands.note: No short game counts unlocks in time (SG:198). The defaults are designer targets of the operator (ticket 19, 2026-11-14): 5 minutes is the first-hour result that ticket T-16 required. The proof row PC4 checks both. The designer sets them.

play_patterns.name: Check-in play (a mobile idle game)
play_patterns.text: The player checks in for short sessions of about 15 minutes. The game pays offline gains while it is closed.
play_patterns.note: The rules of the catalog before 2026-11-14: S06 is core, 1 or more presence gates, and the idle bands of T4.

starter_sets.name: Short active push with a reset and a hard end
starter_sets.rule_note: The short games give the pattern: active play first, automation later, a reset, a hard end (SG:58-71, SG:128-133). They cite no formula, so each variant is a variant that the solver proves (references/design-solver.md).

starter_sets.name: Run on a limit with no reset
starter_sets.proof: Shelldiver (SG:74-84), A Game About Digging a Hole (SG:97-105)
starter_sets.rule_note: The short games give the pattern: a run on a limit, upgrades between runs, no reset, the end at the full tree (SG:76-84, SG:99-105). The laws give no run length with no reset, so the solver takes the simulation path. The scaffold has no writer for S28.full_tree, so the set has the proof class none: no model. With S28.last_step in place of S28.full_tree, the set gives a simulated model.
starter_sets.exception: S04.none is permitted because S29 gives the permanent progress (decision D10).

starter_sets.name: 1 long run with no reset and a hard end
starter_sets.rule_note: The short games give the pattern: 1 run with no reset and no run on a limit, new sites or eras that open in order, a manual action, automation that replaces the manual work, and a hard end (SG:91-95, SG:139-140, SG:146-149). The solver sets R = 1 and proves the growth class (PO1, L1 and L2), the unlock rate (PO10, L3), the time to the hard end (PO12, L8) and the play-test speed (PO13, L9). The rows of the reset loop (PO2 to PO5) are not applicable. The set has the class simulated, not proved: no law covers S24 (the auto-buy) or the idle value of the open game with no reset (PO6).
starter_sets.exception: S04.none is permitted because S28 ends the 1 long run and the run is the permanent progress (decision D11).

answer_rules.note: Do not ask S08 in part C.
Do not ask S09 in part C.
S10 is selected with S10.window. Decision D4.
S09 has nothing to put on the clock.
S13 needs a far system. With no S19, S22 or S23, the skill offers only S13.raised_cap, which the spine S03 raises.
S24 does not run while closed (decision D5).

Decisions D9 and D10. S06 is optional with the default none. The presence gate slot is optional. S04 is optional. S05 (default S05.manual_then_automate), S24 and S28 are core. Ask the targets of part A for continuous: no idle-value targets, the largest gap between purchases in place of the session, and the demo question.
Decision D10. With no reset layer, a run with a permanent tree (S29) or a skill track (S22) is the permanent progress. Rule R1 does not apply.
Decision D10. S28 is core for continuous: the skill does not accept a continuous selection with no hard end.
